peer_positioning.text: IAG ranks top of the network airlines on EBITDA margin ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2025}}), net leverage ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@2025}}), gross leverage ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2025}}) and interest coverage ({{interest_coverage.peer_rank@2025}}).

It also leads on cash generation, with FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} against a peer median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@2025}} and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} against {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@2025}}, ranking {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}} respectively.

Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} puts the company in the middle of the group, and cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} is in line with the peer median, ranking {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}.
Advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2025}}, the weakest of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@2025}}).

watch_items.text: Liquidity: liquidity to revenue fell by {{liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} and undrawn committed facilities were reduced by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2025}}, leaving less headroom as excess cash is returned.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2025}}, the weakest of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@2025}}), a sensitivity if bookings slow.

Unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2025}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2025}}, so the decline in total CASK to {{cask@FY2025}} came with a lower fuel share of costs of {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}}.

Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, in line with the peer median.
